hero.heading: Your homelab, in a Git repo.
hero.lead: Describe your apps, VMs and network in YAML, open a pull request, read the plan, merge. Or push your own code and let Crustates build and deploy it.

capabilities.heading: Every change reviewed, every change reversible.

items.title: Any resource in Git
items.body: Apps, VMs, networks, firewall rules, shares and backup policies are YAML files in your repo.

items.title: Pull, not push
items.body: Spawn polls your repo every few minutes and reacts to webhooks. No port forwarding, no inbound access.

items.title: Plan on every PR
items.body: A dry run through the reconcilers is posted as a PR comment. Merge to apply it.

items.title: Drift detection
items.body: See when the live system no longer matches Git, and choose to revert it, adopt it or just warn.

items.title: Secrets with SOPS
items.body: Encrypt secrets in the repo with SOPS and age. They are decrypted only on your node.

items.title: Image update PRs
items.body: When an app image has a new version, Spawn opens a PR, like Renovate.

items.title: Push to deploy
items.body: Every push to your own app's repo builds on the box and rolls out with health checks.

items.title: PR previews
items.body: Each pull request gets its own preview app at pr-42.blog.crust.internal, removed on close.

items.title: Audit and rollback
items.body: Every change is logged "via git" with the commit. Rolling back is git revert.

how.heading: Two ways to use Git.
how.lead: GitOps keeps your whole setup in a repo. Push-to-deploy builds your own code. Use one, the other or both.

tracks.title: GitOps for your setup
steps: Connect a repo, branch and folder: GitHub App, Forgejo, GitLab, or plain Git with a deploy key.
Open a PR. Spawn posts the dry-run plan as a comment and a check.
Merge. Spawn pulls the commit and the reconcilers apply it, with a snapshot first.
Drift is reported in the console; your prune policy decides what happens.

tracks.title: Push-to-deploy for your code
steps: Connect your app's repo. Spawn detects a Dockerfile, or builds with Railpack if there is none.
Each push builds on the box with BuildKit, with layer caching.
The new version rolls out behind Caddy and must pass its health check.
Pull requests get a preview app; prefer CI? Run a GitHub Actions or Forgejo runner in a microVM.

rows: Same API as console and CLI

example.comment: # Same shape as the API: spec in Git, status on the node
example.ask: "Why did the last deploy of blog fail?" The assistant reads the build log and the commit, and suggests a fix as a PR.

vms.title: What about VMs?
vms.body: Git manages a VM's spec: size, disks, network and cloud-init. What runs inside it stays with cloud-init or a tool like Ansible.

faq.title: Does my homelab need to be reachable from the internet?
faq.body: No. Spawn pulls from your repo. Webhooks are optional and can come through a relay.

faq.title: Is this Flux or Argo CD?
faq.body: No Kubernetes needed. It is built into Crustates and uses the same API as the console.

faq.title: Can I still click things in the console?
faq.body: Yes. Changes made outside Git show up as drift, and you decide whether to adopt or revert them.

faq.title: Which Git hosts work?
faq.body: GitHub with a GitHub App, Forgejo, Gitea and GitLab with webhooks, or any Git server over SSH.
